avoid: Using default ROUND_HALF_EVEN mode; monetary standards require ROUND_HALF_UP
Omitting explicit rounding parameter in quantize() call
Float arithmetic or f-string formatting that loses decimal precision
strategy: Import Decimal and ROUND_HALF_UP from decimal module
Convert all price strings to Decimal objects before summing
Quantize final result with Decimal('0.01') and explicit ROUND_HALF_UP rounding mode
Return as string to preserve two-decimal format
Test boundary cases: sums ending in .005, .015 (rounding-sensitive values)
genes.summary: Monetary calculations fail on precision without explicit rounding mode. Use Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP to handle edge-case summations that rely on banker's rounding sensitivity.

avoid: .lower() on Unicode strings—it misses many case mappings; .casefold() is required
Assuming NFC normalization is sufficient for all Unicode equivalence classes
Reversing normalize/casefold order without verifying all test cases pass
strategy: Normalize both strings with unicodedata.normalize('NFC', string) to canonical form
Apply .casefold() instead of .lower() (casefold handles ß→ss and complex Unicode case mappings)
If tests fail, retry with 'NFKC' form (handles compatibility decomposition) or 'NFD' (decomposed)
Validate with both precomposed and decomposed Unicode sequences in test cases
genes.summary: For Unicode text equality ignoring case: normalize to canonical form, then use .casefold() (not .lower()) for robust cross-encoding comparison.
